problem_statement: Current U.S. election simulations often collapse heterogeneous voter cohorts into aggregate polling averages, weakening state-level uncertainty calibration and making the reasoning from cohort evidence to Electoral College outcomes difficult to audit.

rationale.innovation: Retain GAS-3 hierarchical Group Agents and population-weighted behavior quantization, then expose state-level aggregation, uncertainty and evidence lineage as a falsifiable election pipeline.
reasoning_chain: State outcomes depend on heterogeneous cohorts whose turnout and preference shifts are not represented by one national average.
GAS-3 can preserve cohort hierarchy and population weights while Qwen, called through Bailian, structures scenario evidence and agent rationales.
Aggregating frozen pre-election cohort states yields state scores and Electoral College distributions that can be backtested without leaking post-cutoff evidence.
Calibration and electoral-vote error can falsify whether hierarchical agents improve over polling and uniform-swing baselines.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: Across held-out election cycles and preregistered pre-election cutoffs, GAS-3 will reduce state-level Brier score and electoral-vote MAE versus a uniform national swing baseline.

technical_details.model_runtime: Qwen open-source-family model through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Bailian) API
reproducibility_controls: immutable source SHA-256 and transformation lineage
fixed random seeds, cutoff timestamps and environment versions
agent execution trace plus redacted Qwen/Bailian call receipt
human approval recorded separately from automatic validation

source.source_version: MIT Election Lab U.S. President 1976-2020 source family; normalized 2020 state snapshot
source.pii_assessment: State-level aggregate certified vote totals; no voter-level personal data.
source.redistribution_scope: Normalized aggregate state results with MIT Election Data and Science Lab attribution and version citation.

target.name: Prospective U.S. presidential election panel
target.collection_scope: Multiple historical backtests plus one future U.S. presidential-election cycle, with state-level snapshots frozen at preregistered dates before Election Day.
target.unit_of_analysis: election cycle x state/DC x timestamp x de-identified voter cohort
planned_features: certified historical vote totals and electoral votes
timestamped polls with sample size, mode, sponsor and uncertainty
state demographics and turnout priors from authoritative public statistics
campaign events, endorsements and economic context with provenance
GAS-3 Group Agent states, weights and state win probabilities
target.sampling_strategy: Backtest by holding out complete election cycles; for prospective evaluation, freeze inputs at fixed pre-election horizons and never train on post-cutoff evidence.
target.consent_and_privacy: Use aggregate public election and polling records; do not ingest identifiable voter records. Document every source version and applicable redistribution term.
quality_controls: pre-register inclusion/exclusion rules and primary metrics
version data, code, prompts, Qwen model id and random seeds
retain immutable raw-data hashes and transformation lineage
cross-check totals against certified state results
report calibration and uncertainty, not only winner labels

paper_title: Auditable Hierarchical Group-Agent Simulation for State-Level U.S. Election Forecasting

paper_abstract.background: Aggregate election forecasts underrepresent cohort heterogeneity and hide the derivation of state-level uncertainty.
paper_abstract.methods: We propose a GAS-3 pipeline with hierarchical voter-cohort agents, population-weighted state aggregation, Qwen/Bailian evidence structuring and leakage-safe historical backtests.
paper_abstract.expected_results: We expect improved calibration and lower electoral-vote error than uniform-swing and regularized polling baselines; failure on preregistered metrics will reject the hypothesis.

methods.name: Evidence freeze
methods.procedure: Freeze certified returns, polls and contextual evidence at preregistered cutoffs.

methods.name: Group Agent construction
methods.procedure: Build hierarchical voter cohorts and population weights without identifiable voter records.

methods.name: Scenario execution
methods.procedure: Run Qwen/Bailian-assisted group interactions and preserve every agent/action trace.

methods.name: State aggregation
methods.procedure: Aggregate cohort scores into state predictions and Electoral College totals with calibration.

baselines.name: Uniform national swing
baselines.description: Apply one national shift to historical state margins.

baselines.name: Regularized polling model
baselines.description: Fit a leakage-safe state logistic model on frozen poll aggregates.

metrics.name: Brier score
metrics.definition: Mean squared error of state Republican win scores.

metrics.name: Electoral-vote MAE
metrics.definition: Absolute error in party Electoral College totals.

metrics.name: State accuracy
metrics.definition: Correct winner labels across states and DC.

experiments.split_strategy: Leave complete election cycles out; freeze all prospective inputs before each evaluation cutoff.
experiments.decision_rule: Support only if GAS-3 lowers Brier score and electoral-vote MAE versus the preregistered primary baseline with paired 95% intervals excluding zero.

results.interpretation: The GAS-3 frontend/result contract executed across 50 states plus DC. Because the supplied display priors may derive from the same historical result, these metrics validate wiring and aggregation only.
results.claim_scope: Historical engineering reconstruction; no prospective predictive-validity claim.
